title: Lull-to-Peak Warmup Runbook & Shift Rotations (Apr 2028) - Scratch
content:
Purpose:
Quick practical runbook for warming traffic from lull -> peak during launches, including staggered warmup percentages, telemetry thresholds, and shift rotations. Scratchpad — not finalized. Use this to coordinate ops + SRE + oncall for 48h window around deploy.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API and Dedicated pools (not private on-prem packaging).
- Assumes feature is behind routing flag and can be throttled by percent-of-traffic.
- Primary goal: avoid cold-start latency and model-routing thrash while scaling batch/cache behavior.

Assumptions / constraints:
- Deployment time: 2028-04-14 18:00 UTC (example) -- adjust in calendar.
- Primary region: us-west1, secondary: eu-west1.
- Autoscale warmup disabled for first 30m; manual step policy used.
- Canary slice: 0.5% initial, then ramp with 10m increments.

Quick TL;DR checklist (copy into ticket checklist):
- [ ] Feature flag ready and smoke-test route mapped (dev -> canary).
- [ ] Canary capacity verified against expected rps (bench PR link above).
- [ ] Observability dashboard pinned to release watchlist.
- [ ] Runbook pages shared in #release-orchestra and standup posted.
- [ ] Pager rotations confirmed and escalation ladder annotated.

48h pre-launch (owner: release lead)
- confirm capacity reservations for dedicated pools (ticket RL-1234).
- verify canary config in routing service (svc-config PR linked).
- prewarm job scheduled for cache priming (notes: small synthetic prefix set).
- telemetry baseline snapshot captured (save to /dashboards/release-baseline).
- sanity smoke scripts in CI green, attach artifacts.

24h pre-launch (owner: SRE)
- incremental load test at 25% expected peak for 15m. capture latency p50/p95/p99.
- run KV cache priming in us-west1 and eu-west1.
- confirm fallback variant (quantized model) cold-start times.
- update runbook contact list (oncall + subject matter experts).

4h pre-launch
- brief ops: schedule 2hr preflight stand (15m).
- lock deployment window in calendar + notify CS and support.
- enable extended telemetry retention for 6h post-launch (debug traces).

Launch warmup timeline (pattern: exponential ramp with verification gates)
- T0 (deploy complete): route 0.5% traffic for 10m -> quick smoke; check 5 golden queries.
- T0+10m: if smoke OK, 2% for 15m -> run synthetic load at 20rps.
- T0+25m: 5% for 20m -> check batching heatmap and GPU utilization.
- T0+45m: 15% for 30m -> evaluate latency SLOs and error rates.
- T0+75m: 35% for 30m -> check memory/KV cache hit ratios.
- T0+105m: 65% for 30m -> begin ramp to 100% if steady.
- T0+135m: 100% steady (monitor 2h).

Notes on percent policy:
- If p50 increases > 2x baseline OR p95 > baseline + 400ms -> pause ramp, revert to previous step, open incident channel.
- If error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m -> pause ramp.
- If GPU utilization > 90% sustained -> enable burst nodes or throttle via routing policy.

Telemetry signals (dash panels to watch)
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 by route/model variant.
- Errors: 4xx/5xx split, model runtime exceptions.
- Resource: GPU util, memory, disk i/o.
- Serving metrics: batch size distribution, kv-cache hit rate, queue length.
- Business: failed user transactions, billing anomalies.

Concrete alarm thresholds (first-pass, tune later)
- p95 > baseline + 400ms -> alert to #release-orchestra and page SRE.
- 5xx rate > 0.2% over 3m -> page oncall.
- kv-cache-hit < 65% -> warn channel (investigate cache priming).
- batch size median < expected -> warn (affects cost/latency).

Shift rotations (people + roles)
- Release lead (RL): Maya Thompson (owner) — coordinates cross-team.
- Deployment engineer (DE): Ethan Liu — executes deploy and routing flips.
- Oncall SRE (OC): primary shift for launch 18:00-02:00 UTC: Sofia Ramirez. backup: Diego Nguyen.
- Observability SME (OBS): TBD (assign from observability team).
- Support liaison (CS): assign a support rep for first 4h window.

Suggested rotation blocks (24h coverage post-launch)
- Block A 18:00-02:00 UTC: RL + DE + OC (primary) + OBS.
- Block B 02:00-10:00 UTC: handover note + reduced staffing (DE on-call remote).
- Block C 10:00-18:00 UTC: RL returns for wrap and partner comms.

Handover checklist (on shift change)
- summary of last hour events and current step.
- screenshot of key dashboards + link.
- known mitigations in flight (traffic throttle, model swap).
- actions not yet completed and owner.

Rollback decision matrix (quick)
- Rollback if any of:
  - sustained p95 > baseline + 800ms for 10m,
  - 5xx > 1% for 5m,
  - critical feature regression found in golden queries.
- Rollback process:
  - Step 1: pause routing ramp, move all traffic to fallback variant if available.
  - Step 2: issue rollback via deployment pipeline, tag release as reverted.
  - Step 3: postmortem stub created and initial triage within 2 business hours.

Release notes draft (to be cleaned for external consumption)
- Title: gradual rollout of adaptive-quant routing for multi-variant serving (Apr 2028)
- Summary: enable intelligent routing that prefers low-latency variants while allowing fallbacks. Improves median latency for conversational flows by ~15% in internal tests.
- User impact: most users see no change; a subset of traffic will be routed to a quantized variant (~0.5% -> full).
- Admin notes: new routing flag `adaptive_quant_v2` under feature flags. Operators can roll back via routing-service console.
- Known issues: occasional KV-cache cold misses on first warmup window; throttling may reduce batch sizes temporarily.

Post-launch ops (first 24h)
- 0-2h: watch for transient errors, capture 5 golden query traces, attach to ticket RL-1234.
- 2-6h: compare key metrics to baseline, watch for creeping errors.
- 6-24h: confirm stability, disable extended retention, snapshot dashboards and save artifacts.

Postmortem / followups (owners)
- Performance tuning: investigate batch size oscillations (owner: serving-runtime).
- Observability: add KV-cache warmup panel to default release dashboard (owner: observability).
- Developer docs: update rollout guide with step-by-step warmup recipe (owner: release-engineering).

Open questions / TODOs:
- assign observability SME for this launch (SRE leads: @sre-leads).
- confirm support liaison and customer comm plan (CS).
- should we automate the ramp steps as a single pipeline job? pros/cons - (automation effort vs human gate).
- runbook: add exact CLI commands for routing flips (TODO: Ethan to paste).

Notes to self / quick scribbles:
- consider smoothing percentages more (0.5,1,3,8,20,50,100) vs current plan — maybe less jumpy for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- synthetic golden queries should include edge-case long context.
- remember to mute noisy non-actionable alerts for launch window (list to update).

Links / references:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/Warmup+Playbook+Home
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RL-1234
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/948
- Slack: #release-orchestra (thread pinned)

Appendix: compact hourly calendar (example UTC)
- 2028-04-14 16:00: preflight stand (30m)
- 2028-04-14 17:30: final signoff
- 2028-04-14 18:00: deploy start (T0)
- 18:00-18:10: 0.5% canary smoke
- 18:10-18:25: 2% verification
- 18:25-18:45: 5% verification
- 18:45-19:15: 15% verification
- 19:15-19:45: 35% verification
- 19:45-20:15: 65% verification
- 20:15+: 100% (observe 2h)

End of scratch notes. Clean up and formalize into release brief once SME assignments complete.

--Maya T.
